definitions.explanation: the curved, raised part on the bottom of the foot between the heel and the ball

examples.japanese: {土踏|つちふ}まずが{痛|いた}い。
{土踏|つちふ}まずの{高|たか}い{靴|くつ}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I chose shoes with good arch support.

examples.japanese: {扁平足|へんぺいそく}で{土踏|つちふ}まずがない。
examples.english: I have flat feet and no arch.

notes:
BODY PART:
{土踏|つちふ}まず literally means "doesn't touch the ground" ({土|つち} = ground, {踏|ふ}む = to step on, ず = negative). It refers to the arch of the foot that doesn't touch the ground when standing.

MEDICAL TERMS:
- {扁平足|へんぺいそく} - flat feet (no arch)
- {偏平足|へんぺいそく} - alternate writing for flat feet
- {ハイアーチ|はいあーち} - high arch

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土踏|つちふ}まずが{発達|はったつ}する - for the arch to develop
- {土踏|つちふ}まずを{サポート|さぽーと}する - to support the arch

RELATED:
- {足|あし} - foot/leg
- {足裏|あしうら} - sole of the foot
- {かかと} - heel
